jobs.title: Senior Project Manager, Biologist or Environmental Scientist
jobs.description:
Find your path and enjoy the journey at Haley & Aldrich
. With us, you’ll tackle clients’ most meaningful challenges in the built and natural environments – and, in turn, build stronger communities. You’ll work with teams of passionate colleagues, driven by a commitment to technical excellence and continuous learning.

As a company, we aim to build a world where communities go beyond resilience, embracing change as an opportunity to enhance safety, well-being, and quality of life. Join us to accelerate this vision and your professional development.

We are looking to add new talent to our growing team! We are currently seeking an experienced Senior Project Manager, Biologist or Environmental Scientist
to work in a business development and technical lead role with highly skilled professionals on diverse project teams in a dynamic environment. This is an excellent opportunity to join a growing group and company and get involved in a variety of projects for a diverse range of clients. This is a full-time
position located in one of our Michigan or Ohio ( Rockford / Ann Arbor, MI, or Independence, Miamisburg, Cincinnati, OH)
offices.

Duties/Responsibilities

In this position, you will :

Lead and assist with identifying new client opportunities while developing internal and external networks into a book of business.
Lead business development opportunities to assist our northwest region’s natural resources and permitting - growth initiatives.
Assist with the development and diversification of natural resources and permitting services in the northwest region across multiple markets (Energy, Real Estate, Industrial, Remediation…).
Lead and assist with the execution of natural resources and permitting project work through individual contribution and delegation to lower-level staff
Develop technical scopes of work and proposals within your area of expertise, connecting your work with other project components to support client goals. Recognize when conditions require modifications to meet client- or regulatory-specific requirements.
Demonstrate and apply knowledge of proper jurisdictional codes, regulations, and professional standards of practice to assigned project work.
Coach, mentor, and support staff to facilitate knowledge transfer and ensure high-quality execution of project tasks, technical reports, and deliverables.
Use developing skills to be visible in your specialty area by giving internal and external technical presentations and attending external networking events to identify business development opportunities.
Play a significant leadership role in performing technical evaluations and developing conceptual site models on environmental, natural resource, and land use permitting projects.
Lead the development of proposals and technical reporting efforts supporting natural resource, permitting/compliance, other related projects, and assist with development of documentation reporting standards.
Work with the appropriate staff to support the design and development of restoration and mitigation design plans on various aquatic and habitat projects.
Perform or oversee field implementation of technical resource studies, restoration/mitigation design development and implementation along with construction oversight, as needed.
Plan and perform all work in accordance with company and client health and safety protocols.
Demonstrate the company’s foundational safety behaviors.

Skills/Experience

Minimum Skills and Requirements :

Bachelor’s degree in Biology, Environmental Science, Natural Resources, or related field.
Minimum of 15 years related experience including 5 years of Project Management.
Professional Wetland Scientist (PWS) certification preferred.
Experience with local, state and federal permitting, natural resource management (species surveys and documentation), regulations/requirements and experience with wetlands in the Mid-West Michigan or Ohio regions a must.
Experience with Ohio Power Siting Board (OPSB) projects.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including verbally presenting project information to peers, stakeholders, and clients.
Desire to advance skills in your area of expertise to become more visible in the industry.
Environmental design and contract package development experience.
Working knowledge of regulatory frameworks pertinent to the work.

Preferred Skills

Master’s degree in Natural Resource, Environmental Science, Biology, or related field.
Experience conducting permitting/compliance with local, state, and federal regulations related to wetlands and other natural resources. Including state (SEPA) and federal (NEPA) documentation preparation and compliance.
Experience conducting wetland and habitat evaluations to determine resource liabilities & make recommendations on permits, design plans and mitigation requirements to achieve compliance.
OSHA 40-Hour HAZWOPER training and refresher updates.

The salary range for this position in Ann Arbor, MI; Rockford, MI; Cincinnati, OH; Miamisburg, OH; and Independence, OH is $130,000 - 150,000 annually
. Actual compensation will be based upon a variety of factors such as education, related work experience, certificates, skills, and current market conditions. Haley & Aldrich reviews salary ranges each quarter to assess competitiveness with the market.

About Haley & Aldrich

Haley & Aldrich is committed to solving our clients’ most meaningful challenges in the built and natural environments. Our team of 1,000+ engineers and scientists across the United States draws inspiration from one mission: to work closely with clients as they navigate change to create safer, more robust places to live and work. Since our founding in 1957, organizations across the public and private sectors have relied on us for technical excellence and empathetic leadership that achieve results and secure a thriving tomorrow. Find us at haleyaldrich.com and LinkedIn .

Haley & Aldrich is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applications will receive consideration for employment without regard to gender, race, age, disability, veteran, or any other legally protected status. We offer excellent career growth, a highly competitive total compensation plan, and a solid benefits package. Interested candidates should apply on our Careers page.

Note to external search firms:
Haley & Aldrich does not accept unsolicited resumes and will not be obligated to pay a placement fee for unsolicited resumes. Please do not send resumes to Haley & Aldrich employees. Please work through a Talent Acquisition Manager.

jobs.description:
Shape Your World

At Alcoa, you will become an essential part of our purpose: to turn raw potential into real progress. The way we see it, every Alcoan is a work-shaper, team-shaper, idea-shaper & world-shaper.

This is your opportunity to help shape the future of sustainability with world-changing innovations and low-carbon technologies. Become a valued part of the team that’s shaping the future of aluminium, revolutionising the way the world lives, builds, moves and flies. Be part of it and shape your world.

About The Role

Join our Mining Environmental team as a Plant Production Specialist at Huntly, where you will help improve seed use and plant establishment outcomes across Alcoa’s rehabilitation and remediation programs. This role is based at Huntly Central working a Monday to Friday roster.

Reporting to the Plant Production Superintendent, you will combine your knowledge of seed biology, plant production, experimental design and data analysis to support species richness outcomes and help Alcoa meet its rehabilitation completion criteria. You will work closely with internal teams, research providers and external suppliers to turn data and research into practical improvements.

In this role, you will:

Manage and analyse seed, plant production and field data to support informed decision-making.
Implement improvement projects focused on broadcast seed optimisation and tubestock survival.
Coordinate seed and plant production projects with external suppliers and research providers.
Support experimental design, implementation, data analysis and reporting.
Contribute to business system improvements, document control and effective data management.
Complete work with a strong focus on safe project delivery, field activities and collaboration.

What’s On Offer

Attractive remuneration and variable bonus plan.
18 weeks Parental leave for primary caregivers.
One additional paid Alcoa Flexi Day.
My Alcoa Benefits program offering travel, lifestyle, health and wellbeing discounts.
Generous leave entitlements including a leisure a day off every 4-week period.
Salary packaging for a novated car lease, employee share plan and superannuation options.
Connect and be part of a community that celebrates diversity through our employee inclusion groups.

What You Can Bring To The Role

A degree in Environmental Science or an equivalent qualification.
Working knowledge of seed biology, germination and plant growth.
Experience working with inventory management processes and systems.
Knowledge of experimental design and the implementation of research projects.
Strong data management, analysis and reporting capability.
The ability to identify, develop and support practical improvement opportunities.

Additional Information

Interviews may progress prior to the closing date, although all applications will be considered.
You will only be contacted if you are shortlisted for an interview, this process can take up to four weeks from the closing date.

Be part of shaping our organisation and join us in building a legacy of excellence for future generations.

#AlcoaAUS

About the Location

Huntly is one of our two bauxite mines in Western Australia. Established in 1976 and located east of North Dandalup in WA, it is the world’s second largest bauxite mine, supplying ore to Alcoa’s Pinjarra alumina refinery. Bauxite ore from Alcoa’s Huntly and Willowdale mines helps to produce almost half of Australia’s alumina and approximately 19 per cent of Australia’s aluminium. Our workplace is an inclusive and respectful environment, where we embrace change, new ideas and equal opportunity to succeed.

We are values led, vision driven and united by our purpose of transforming raw potential into real progress.  Our commitments to Inclusion, Diversity & Equity include providing trusting workplaces that are safe, respectful and inclusive of all individuals, free from discrimination, bullying and harassment and that our workplaces reflect the diversity of the communities in which we operate.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Environmental Compliance
jobs.description:
Company Description

Veolia in North America is the top-ranked environmental company in the United States for three consecutive years, and the country’s largest private water operator and technology provider as well as hazardous waste and pollution treatment leader. It offers a full spectrum of water, waste, and energy management services, including water and wastewater treatment, commercial and hazardous waste collection and disposal, energy consulting and resource recovery. Veolia helps commercial, industrial, healthcare, higher education and municipality customers throughout North America. Headquartered in Boston, Veolia has more than 10,000 employees working at more than 350 locations across North America.

Position Purpose

The Senior Director of Environmental Compliance is responsible for providing strategic leadership and oversight of Veolia Water New Jersey’s (VWNJ) environmental compliance programs, ensuring compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local environmental regulations, in alignment with corporate objectives and operational priorities, while advancing public health protection, environmental stewardship, operational excellence, and continuous improvement. This position provides executive oversight of all environmental compliance activities related to air, drinking water, wastewater, stormwater, waste management, hazardous materials, spill prevention and response, environmental permitting, emergency preparedness, and environmental auditing.

This position leads the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of the Company's environmental compliance management systems, environmental governance framework, and regulatory compliance programs across all VWNJ operations. The Senior Director provides oversight of all laboratory analysis required to demonstrate compliance, including outside laboratory services and the Haworth WTP laboratory.

The Senior Director serves as the organization's subject matter expert for environmental compliance, environmental permitting, drinking water quality, wastewater treatment compliance, environmental management systems, and environmental regulatory relations. The role partners closely with other functional areas including, operations, engineering, legal, finance, strategic relations, etc., to identify environmental risks, implement mitigation strategies, and ensure consistent compliance across all operations.

Primary Duties/Responsibilities

Lead, empower, and mentor a direct team of environmental professionals, driving cohesive collaboration and operational alignment across all functional disciplines within the position's scope (including Operations, Engineering, Legal, and Finance).
Serve as a strategic leader with external regulatory agencies, effectively interpreting complex regulations and guidelines to advocate for approaches that balance strict regulatory compliance with exceptional customer service and operational/business realities.
Provide environmental compliance leadership for VWNJ. Ensure alignment with corporate objectives and operational priorities.
Provide strategic oversight of compliance programs related to all applicable federal, state, and local environmental regulations, including requirements administered by the EPA and applicable state environmental agencies.
Monitor legislative and regulatory developments and communicate impacts to business leadership. Lead development of comments for submission during public comment period for draft regulatory requirements. Interpret emerging regulatory requirements and develop implementation strategies to ensure organizational readiness.
Support development of policies related to water treatment operations, laboratory quality assurance, and regulatory reporting.
Lead the design, implementation, and continual improvement of VWNJ’s environmental compliance management systems.
Lead environmental due diligence activities supporting capital projects and new business initiatives.
Evaluate environmental impacts associated with operational activities and infrastructure investments.
Direct internal environmental assessments and support external regulatory inspections. Oversee development, implementation, and closure of corrective action plans.
Lead VWNJ environmental auditing and compliance assurance programs.
Monitor environmental performance trends and ensure timely resolution of compliance issues.
Oversee environmental permitting activities across all operations.
Ensure timely submission of required regulatory reports and environmental compliance documentation.
Ensure maintenance of systems supporting environmental permits, compliance obligations, inspections, reporting, and regulatory commitments.
Provide oversight of environmental emergency preparedness and response programs.
Direct environmental incident investigations, including spill response and root cause analyses.
Serve as liaison with environmental regulatory agencies.
Build productive relationships with regulators, industry associations, and external stakeholders.
Represent the organization during inspections, audits, enforcement actions, and compliance negotiations.
Establish departmental goals, performance expectations, succession planning, and employee development initiatives.
Allocate resources to support business priorities and regulatory obligations.
Foster collaboration across Operations, Engineering, Legal,Finance, and Corporate leadership.
Develop departmental strategic plans, budgets, and resource forecasts.
Establish and monitor environmental performance objectives, key performance indicators (KPIs), and reporting metrics.
Recommend process improvements that enhance compliance, operational reliability, sustainability, and financial performance.
Support corporate sustainability and environmental stewardship initiatives.

Work Environment

Participation in environmental emergency response activities and on-call leadership, as required.
Combination of office and field environments, including visits to treatment facilities, construction sites, laboratories, and industrial operations.
Ability to conduct field inspections and work in varying environmental conditions while utilizing appropriate personal protective equipment.

Qualifications

Education/Experience/Background:

Bachelor's degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Chemistry, Biology, or a related technical discipline.
Master's degree preferred.
Minimum of 12 years of progressively responsible environmental compliance experience within a regulated utility, environmental services, industrial, manufacturing, or infrastructure organization.
Minimum of 7 years of leadership experience managing environmental professionals and cross-functional teams.
Demonstrated experience leading environmental compliance programs across multiple operating locations.
Experience interacting with federal and state regulatory agencies.
Experience developing and implementing environmental compliance management systems.
Experience supporting environmental due diligence, capital projects, and business development preferred.

Knowledge/Skills/Abilities

Working knowledge of federal, state, and local environmental regulations, including the Safe Drinking Water Act, Clean Water Act, Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA), Clean Air Act, and related environmental permitting requirements.
Knowledge of drinking water treatment, water chemistry, wastewater operations, hazardous materials management, and environmental risk management.
Strong understanding of environmental auditing, compliance assurance, and regulatory reporting.
Working knowledge of environmental compliance management systems and continuous improvement methodologies.
Experience developing environmental compliance strategies, policies, and governance frameworks.
Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.
Excellent communication and presentation skills.
Proven ability to influence senior leaders and build effective relationships across diverse stakeholder groups.
Strong project management and organizational leadership capabilities.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office/Google applications and environmental compliance management systems.

Additional Information

Pay Range:
$180000 to $200000 Per Year.

Benefits:
Veolia’s comprehensive benefits package includes paid time off policies, as well as health, dental, vision, life insurance, savings accounts, tuition reimbursement, paid volunteering and more. In addition, employees are also entitled to participate in an employer sponsored 401(k) plan, to save for retirement. Pay and benefits for employees represented by a union are outlined in their collective bargaining agreement.

Sick leave – 56 hours; Observed Holidays – 11 days; Vacation – Flexible Time Off

Eligible for up to 20% Annual Performance Bonus

Job Description

Expression of Interest - Engineers | Technicians | Project Managers | Environmental Scientists

Bring your expertise. Build something meaningful— and a great life — in Bundaberg.

Are you an experienced technical or project professional looking for greater influence, meaningful regional work and the opportunity to grow your leadership career?

Join GHD’s close-knit Bundaberg team and help shape projects that support communities across the Wide Bay. You’ll enjoy the visibility and connection of a regional office, backed by the capability, opportunities and multidisciplinary expertise of GHD’s wider Queensland and global network.

GHD is seeking Expressions of Interest
from experienced professionals interested in joining our Bundaberg team and leading our growth and presence across the Wide Bay region.

We’re deliberately keeping our search broad. Your project management or technical background could be in transport, civil, water, structural, electrical, environment or another technical discipline. What matters most is your ability to bring strong consulting experience, work closely with clients and contribute to both project delivery and business growth.

Build your career, and a great life, in Bundaberg

A move to Bundaberg could mean creating more space for what matters while continuing to work on meaningful projects, build trusted client relationships and grow your professional influence.

Bundaberg combines the serenity of coastal living with a strong sense of community and connection. The region is the closest mainland gateway to Lady Musgrave and Lady Elliot islands — two of the Southern Great Barrier Reef’s finest coral cays — and is surrounded by beaches, mangroves, and other ecosystems that support diverse marine life.

The region also offers the everyday essentials that make relocation easier: accessibility to Brisbane, modern schools, growing recreational opportunities, and high-quality healthcare facilities and upgrades. A diversified regional economy supports employment, investment and a lifestyle that guarantees a rewarding alternative to the hustle and bustle of major-city living.

At GHD, you’ll become part of a close-knit local team where your contribution will be visible and valued. You’ll work alongside people with deep regional knowledge while being widely supported by multidisciplinary colleagues across Queensland and GHD’s global network. It’s an opportunity to build local relationships, broaden your experience and make a lasting impact on the communities around you.

Discover what life in the Bundaberg region could offer you.

What could your opportunity look like?

Depending on your experience and background, you could join us as an Engineer, Technician, Project Manager or Environmental Scientist. In our Bundaberg team, you’ll have the opportunity to work across disciplines, build strong relationships with regional clients and play a visible role in the continued growth of our Wide Bay business.

Regional consulting can offer broader exposure and greater influence. You may find yourself working more closely with clients, contributing across the full project lifecycle and helping shape opportunities from their earliest stages — while still having access to the technical depth and career pathways of a global professional services company.

You may already be an established senior professional, or you may be ready to broaden your influence, take on greater client and commercial responsibility and continue developing towards future leadership opportunities.

This opportunity isn’t defined by a single technical discipline. We’re looking for the right capability, consulting mindset and client orientation to complement our Bundaberg team and contribute to our continued growth across the region.

What You’ll Bring

We’d like to hear from you if you bring:

5 plus years’ experience in consulting, technical delivery or project management
A background in engineering, environment, project management or another relevant technical discipline
Strong client-facing and relationship-building capability
A commercial mindset and an interest in identifying and developing opportunities
The ability and willingness to contribute directly to project delivery
A collaborative approach and the ability to work across disciplines, projects and locations
An interest in contributing to the continued growth of our Bundaberg business
The ambition to continue developing your career and potentially move into broader leadership over time
Relevant professional accreditation for your discipline, such as RPEQ and/or CPEng, or working towards attaining accreditation where applicable

You don’t need to already know the Queensland market. We’re interested in professionals who bring the right consulting and client-focused approach, valuable experience and a willingness to collaborate with colleagues who have strong local market knowledge.

About Us

At Onterris, we build careers grounded in purpose, responsibility and real-world impact.

“For Planet and Progress” is our north star that guides everything we do. We believe environmental responsibility and human progress are interconnected, interwoven and international. Our scientists, engineers, field teams, consultants and professionals collaborate across disciplines and geographies, guiding industries and governments, ensuring that communities and environments thrive.

When you join us, you’re not just forging a career, you’re joining a movement. A movement for better thinking, smarter solutions and lasting impact.

Together, we will advance our way of life and protect the integrity of our environment every step of the way.

A Day in the Life

A Junior Environmental Scientist
participates as a member of an emergency response team to conduct environmental sampling and data collection. In performing such duties, a Junior Environmental Scientist will conduct research or perform investigations for the purpose of identifying, abating, or eliminating sources of pollutants or hazards that affect either the environment or the health of the population. Utilizing their knowledge of various scientific disciplines, they may collect, synthesize, study, report, and act based on data derived from measurements or observations of air, food, soil, water, and other sources. The successful candidate will apply scientific methodology for analysis of risk assessments and industrial hygiene applications to ensure the client’s expectations are met. All Junior Environmental Scientist’s shall maintain a response bag with company issued PPE and appropriate work clothing. This role is also subject to on-call rotation for emergency response and frequent, extended travel. The on-call rotation duties may extend to satellite offices as necessary. Travel on a moment’s notice may extend further than just the on-call rotation i.e. in the event a response requires more staffing support.

The compensation range for this role is $38,500 to $44,600
commensurate with experience, skills, and geographic location.

To thrive in this role, you’ll be comfortable taking ownership of the following responsibilities:

Immediate availability for extended travel and emergency response at client’s request
Maintain, calibrate and mobilize equipment appropriate for an emergency response
Gather and analyze samples from various sources of potential contamination
Perform monitoring and sampling activities according to the prescribed methods
Compile, review and summarize scientific/technical data and literature; and,
Completion of 40-hour HAZWOPER training in accordance with 29 CFR 1910.120 within first three weeks of hire date
Possession of DISA & TWIC clearances within 3 months of hire date
Completion of all designated safety requirements within first month of hire date; and
Perform other duties as assigned

These requirements reflect the knowledge, skills and abilities that help you do your best work here.

Bachelor's degree in Biology, Environmental Engineering, Environmental, Health and Safety,
Industrial Hygiene, Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Toxicology or other related science
1 to 3 years of experience in a related field may be substituted in lieu of a degree
Advanced computer skills in a Windows-based platform is a must
The ability to learn various software and complying with administrative duties (time sheets/expense reports)
Ability to work independently and with minimal supervision
Ability to respond in a timely manner to all communications from his/her supervisor
Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships within a matrix reporting structure
Ability to understand and follow written and verbal directions
Possess strong verbal and written communication skills in the English language
Ability to complete HAZWOPER certification
Ability to obtain and maintain DISA clearance
Ability to obtain TWIC clearance
Current driver’s license
Ability to obtain a passport
Completion of all job specific OSHA training
Ability to comply with all job specific OSHA requirements, including the wear of a respirator
Possess excellent problem-solving and analytical skills with careful attention to detail being critical
Possess a high degree of personal initiative and responsibility for work assigned
Ability to understand and follow written and verbal directions
Demonstrate excellent verbal and written communication skills in the English language; and,
Ability to work overtime and on weekends

Work Environment And Physical Requirements

We may provide reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities, consistent with applicable law, to support performance of the essential functions.

Sitting, standing, and walking

Overhead lifting of over 20 pounds
Bending, stooping, climbing ladders and crawling
Long hours involving overtime and weekends as necessary
Keyboarding/typing
